reason: The giant can gravitationally redirect the distant icy bodies, addressing the first goal.
expectation: I expect some icy bodies to be sent inward, though their exact paths are uncertain.

alternatives.reason: This might address the leftover debris, but I want to follow the old ice first.

effect: The giant sent a population of icy bodies inward, where different members can have different encounters.
reaction: The separate possible fates make me curious about what happens in the warm inner system.
reason: Following the inward ice into warm space directly continues the first goal.
expectation: I expect some of the ice to turn into gas and release dust, as in the earlier warm-disk encounter.

alternatives.reason: A collision with a rocky world is another possible fate, but I want to see the warming first.

effect: The inward ice released gas and dust in the warm inner system, while a cold remnant can remain.
reaction: The immense, thin cloud trailing a small remnant is a striking image.
reason: I want to follow another possible fate of the inward icy bodies by bringing them near the rocky worlds.
expectation: Some icy bodies may strike rocky worlds, though I don't know what the encounter will leave.

alternatives.reason: Warming the leftover debris might address the other goal, but I want to follow the ice first.

effect: Some inward ice struck and cratered the rocky worlds, completing the first goal without necessarily delivering oceans.
reaction: The distinction between impact delivery and forming an ocean is useful.
reason: I want to follow the remaining debris in warm space to address the second goal.
expectation: I expect the warm environment to alter or disperse some of the debris, though its exact fate is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: The giant could also redirect the debris, but I want to see what happens among the rocky worlds first.

effect: Repeated collisions turned some leftover stones into fine dust, revealing one fate of material between the planets.
reaction: The gradual breakdown into dust makes physical sense.
reason: Combining the two dust sources follows the material that missed the worlds.
expectation: I expect dust from the warming ice and colliding stones to mix in the inner system, though its subsequent fate is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: The giant may redirect leftover debris, but I want to follow the newly formed dust first.

effect: The two dust sources mingled and scattered starlight, completing the remaining goal.
reaction: The faint glow is a satisfying way to bring the two material histories together.

mostWorthwhile.text: Combining the dust sources was most worthwhile: it connected the icy bodies and broken stones in a visible result.

leastWorthwhile.text: Warming the inward ice felt somewhat repetitive after the similar encounter in the earlier history, though the trailing cloud was evocative.

surprise.text: I liked the distinction that icy impacts can vaporize and lose material without necessarily delivering an ocean.

arbitrary.text: No action felt especially arbitrary; the available combinations had understandable physical purposes.

continue.text: I might continue to see how the system evolves, though another sequence of familiar dust and ice encounters would be less compelling.
